facts.statement: 45 US states and DC expressly require a criminal background check before a driver can be activated on a transportation network company (TNC) platform; several states (e.g. Illinois, Texas) require the check to cover at least 7 years of criminal and driving history.
facts.source_title: States Address Background Checks for Rideshare Drivers

facts.statement: Some states require drivers to be periodically re-screened rather than checked only at signup - e.g. Colorado requires a renewed criminal history record check at least every 5 years for a driver to remain active on the platform.
facts.source_title: States Address Background Checks for Rideshare Drivers

facts.statement: Under ADA Title III, a driver cannot refuse a rider because of a disability or a mobility device that reasonably fits in the vehicle, cannot charge more for stowing the device, and must provide reasonable assistance stowing it; the matching/dispatch logic must not systematically disadvantage riders who flag an accessibility need.
facts.source_title: The ADA and Accessible Ground Transportation

facts.statement: State TNC insurance laws mandate different minimum coverage for distinct trip phases - e.g. New York requires at least $75,000/$150,000/$25,000 (bodily injury per person/per accident/property damage) while a driver is logged in and waiting for a request, and California requires $1,000,000 primary coverage once a ride is active - so the system must track and record which phase a driver is in at any time.
facts.source_title: FAQs About Transportation Network Companies (Ride Sharing)

facts.statement: Real-time GPS location data collected during a trip is personal data and must be collected under informed consent with data minimisation, consistent with GDPR/CCPA-style requirements.

Personal auto insurance policies commonly exclude coverage while a driver's app is on but no ride has yet been accepted (the 'insurance gap' period); state TNC laws close this by mandating minimum liability coverage for that period too, so the platform must not treat 'app on, waiting' as an uninsured or unlogged state.
facts.source_title: FAQs About Transportation Network Companies (Ride Sharing)
